digest.top_line: EANO radiation necrosis consensus: 53/57 statements ≥80% agreement, perfusion MRI + amino acid PET to call RN, bev when steroid-dependent >4wk on dex ≥8 mg/day.
digest.tldr: CNS carries the day alone, and it's a document not a trial: no Level 1 evidence anywhere, so treat symptoms not images. Practical for RT planning are the dose-volume thresholds (SRS V12Gy ~10 cm³ → 5-10% symptomatic RN; cumulative re-irradiation EQD2 >130 Gy → up to 25%) and the higher-risk flag for SRS with dual checkpoint blockade or ADCs.

sites.intro: One consensus document, no efficacy endpoint: its value to an RT reader is the constraint table and the diagnostic algorithm, not a result.

studies.name: EANO Consensus Statement on Radiation Necrosis
studies.tldr: Delphi consensus, 53/57 statements ≥80% agreement: perfusion MRI + amino acid PET to call RN, bevacizumab for steroid-refractory.
details: 🔍 Three-round Delphi, 20 experts (15 initial + 5 added in round 1), consensus threshold ≥80% on 5-point Likert
🔍 Panel included 3 radiation/clinical oncologists, 4 neuro-oncologists, 4 med oncs, 2 neurosurgeons, neuropathologist, neuroradiologist, nuclear medicine

details.text: 📊 57 statements formulated across epidemiology-pathophysiology (n=8), causes (n=10), imaging (n=10), histopathology (n=9), management (n=20); 53 reached consensus
📐 Dose-volume thresholds for RN risk, verbatim from the causes section

rows: Repeat SRS after prior SRS or WBRT

details.text: 📊 Diagnostic performance by modality (pooled, from the imaging section)
📊 RN incidence 4-30% overall, most series reporting symptomatic RN up to 10%; 4-30% in irradiated gliomas, 5-24% in brain mets

details: 🔍 Timing: 6-24 months post-RT typically, with delayed cases years later; lesion then plateaus 12-24 months on conventional MRI
💊 Steroid-to-bevacizumab trigger: steroid-dependent symptoms >4 weeks needing dexamethasone ≥8 mg/day (87.5% agreement)
💊 No preferred bevacizumab schedule: 5 mg/kg q2w, 7.5 mg/kg q3w, 400 mg fixed q2w, 600 mg fixed q3w all in use, no comparative evidence (87.5% agreement)
🔗 No prospective data show a difference in RN incidence for protons vs photons; end-of-range uncertainty and conformality remain the counterweight to reduced integral dose
⚠️ Increased RN risk flagged when SRS is combined with dual checkpoint blockade (CTLA-4 + PD-1) or antibody-drug conjugates
⚠️ Surgery statement cleared the bar by the narrowest margin in the management table (80.0% agreement); LITT reached 100% but only in round 3
⚠️ No Level 1 evidence anywhere in the document, and only symptom-driven treatment is endorsed: radiological findings alone do not justify treating
⚠️ No definition of radiological response after RN treatment (88.9% agreement), so response assessment in future RN trials has no agreed endpoint

verdict.rationale: Three-round Delphi expert opinion, no efficacy endpoint; authors state Level 1 evidence is absent. Codifies existing practice and names the dose thresholds and treatment triggers.
verdict.audience: Post-cranial-RT pts with a new/enlarging contrast-enhancing lesion, glioma or…

studies.significance: The RT-actionable content is the dose-volume section, not the algorithm: EQD2 below ~40 Gy makes RN uncommon, single-fraction V12Gy ~10 cm³ carries 5-10% symptomatic necrosis, and re-irradiation stays under 10% to cumulative EQD2 100-110 Gy but reaches 25% above 130 Gy. Those numbers gate the fractionate-vs-single-fraction and re-irradiate-vs-not decisions.
studies.monday_clinic: For a post-SRS patient with a new enhancing lesion, this supports adding perfusion MRI and amino acid PET before calling recurrence, and supports bevacizumab once dexamethasone dependence passes 4 weeks at ≥8 mg; it says nothing about treating asymptomatic radiological RN.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Three-round **Delphi** consensus under EANO. 57 statements drafted after literature review, voted on a 5-point Likert scale, consensus prespecified at **≥80% agreement**. **53 of 57** statements reached consensus, with statement adaptation between rounds.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Panel of **20 experts**: 15 volunteers (2 radiation/clinical oncologists, 4 neuro-oncologists, 4 medical oncologists, 2 neurosurgeons, 1 neuropathologist, 1 neuroradiologist, 1 nuclear medicine physician) plus 5 invited to vote from round 1. Clinical scope is cerebral RN after RT for **primary glial or metastatic brain tumors**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: RN is **uncommon below EQD2 ~40 Gy** (α/β 2 Gy for normal brain); above that, risk scales with dose per fraction, total dose, and irradiated volume. Single-session SRS **V12Gy ~10 cm³** maps to a **5-10%** symptomatic necrosis risk; hypofractionated SRT with brain+target **V20Gy (3 fx) or V24Gy (5 fx) <20 cm³** gives **<10%** any necrosis/edema and **<4%** RN needing resection. Re-irradiation: **<10%** to cumulative EQD2 100-110 Gy, **up to 25%** above 130 Gy.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Diagnostic consensus is that **T1 CE MRI alone is insufficient** (100% agreement) and that advanced MRI plus amino acid PET gives the highest accuracy (94.4%). **TBRmean over TBRmax** took until round 3 to reach 100%. Management consensus centres on symptom-triggered treatment, minimum effective dexamethasone, and bevacizumab escalation.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Bevacizumab at RN doses is described as **usually well tolerated**, with wound healing problems and arterial hypertension as the main issues, plus increased DVT and pulmonary embolism risk and a small increase in cerebral hemorrhage or infarction (94.1% agreement).

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents patients with a new or enlarging contrast-enhancing lesion after cranial RT for glioma or brain metastases. Does not represent pseudoprogression in the first months after chemoradiation, or the late enlarging cysts after SRT that the panel considers pathogenetically separate from RN.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Statement-level agreement percentages are published, but the management and imaging tables arrive with row labels and values on separate lines in the source, so several agreement figures cannot be tied to a specific statement with confidence. Panel composition is systemic-heavy relative to the dosimetric content: 8 medical/neuro-oncologists to 3 radiation oncologists.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The document names what is unknown as clearly as what is agreed: no best bevacizumab dose or duration, no defined radiological response criterion, unknown recurrence rate after bevacizumab, undetermined predictors of response. It also flags an ESTRO terminology paper proposing **TRIA** (treatment-related imaging abnormality) as the preferred term, so nomenclature is still moving.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The dose-volume constraints are the transferable part: EQD2 ~40 Gy as the threshold below which RN is uncommon, single-fraction V12Gy ~10 cm³ at 5-10% symptomatic necrosis, and re-irradiation risk climbing from <10% at cumulative EQD2 100-110 Gy to 25% above 130 Gy. These gate hypofractionation and re-irradiation decisions directly.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Bevacizumab is the endorsed escalation once dexamethasone dependence exceeds 4 weeks at ≥8 mg/day, with four dosing schedules in use and no evidence favoring one. Added caution when SRS is combined with dual checkpoint blockade or antibody-drug conjugates, where RN risk may rise.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Resection carries a consensus recommendation whenever feasible without compromising safety, giving both diagnosis and definitive treatment, though it cleared the 80% bar by the narrowest margin of any management statement. LITT is positioned narrowly: treatment-resistant RN that is not surgically resectable.

papers.title: The European Association for Neuro-oncology (EANO) Consensus Statement on Radiation Necrosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Radiation necrosis (RN) complicates neuro-oncological care, mimicking tumor recurrence and lacking high-level evidence for standardized management. Methods A European Association for Neuro-Oncology (EANO) expert panel utilized a three-round Delphi process to create a comprehensive expert opinion document based on the available current scientific evidence. A series of statements, derived from the published literature were created by the experts in each field. Consensus was defined as ≥ 80% agreement using a 5-point Likert scale. Results After three rounds among 20 experts that included adaptation of statements, the Delphi process reached a consensus (≥80% agreement) on 53 statements out of 57. RN occurs in 4% to 30% of patients, typically appearing 6 to 24 months after radiotherapy for primary (glial) or metastatic brain tumors. Experts identified perfusion MRI and amino acid PET as the most suitable imaging modalities for differentiation from tumor recurrence. While histopathology remains the gold standard, identifying viable tumor cells in irradiated gliomas is challenging due to overlapping cytological features with reactive glia. For symptomatic management, corticosteroids may be tried, and bevacizumab is recommended for corticosteroid-refractory cases, with evidence suggesting profound efficacy even at low doses. Surgery is considered effective for rapid symptom relief and definitive diagnosis in accessible lesions. Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy (LITT) can be considered an additional treatment option for symptomatic RN. Conclusions Despite the absence of Level 1 evidence, these Delphi-survey-formulated recommendations provide actionable guidance for clinical practice. There is a need for prospective randomized trials focusing on symptomatic RN.
